correct_completion: she handed it to the manager.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, she handed it to the manager.
acceptable_variants: she then sent it to the manager.
she submitted it to the manager.

options.text: the report was lost somewhere in the office.
options.why_wrong: The participle clause 'having finished' refers to the subject of the main clause, so the main clause must describe the person who finished, not the report itself.

options.text: she will hand it to the manager tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: A future action does not follow logically from 'having finished', which presents the completed action as the one that happened first.

options.text: she handed it to the manager.
she keeps finishing it again and again.
options.why_wrong: Repetition does not match the single completed action expressed by 'having finished', which sets up one clear sequence.

grammar_focus: Perfect participle clauses expressing a completed prior action
explanation: The perfect participle clause describes an action completed before the main verb, so the main clause must be the next action in the sequence and share the same subject. Learners often choose a future or repeated action here, which breaks the logical order of events.
translation: Depois de terminar o relatório, ela o entregou ao gerente.
